text:
noah: Heads-up — I'm seeing a small but steady memory climb on a long streaming repro (tool-loop + streaming chat) on prod-like infra. Starts around 2h in and keeps growing ~30MB/hour. Not spikey, more of a drift.

morgan: ugh. is this the same workload as the pagechain fuzz test you ran?

noah: similar shape. Tool loop that opens many short-lived sessions, appends to chat, uses streaming responses. I repro locally with 24h run: heap grows ~700MB. Attached a quick heap diff from the runtime: `alloc_summary: kv_pages_active=18432 -> 19680, slab_frag_percent=12.4 -> 18.9`

devon: can you paste the small profiler trace? maybe kv residency or pinned pages?

noah: pasted snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] kv_cache: page_allocs=134k page_reclaims=89k page_evictions=4.2k
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] kv_residency: avg_session_pages=48 tail_anchored=1.2k
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] slab: allocs=1.3M frees=1.28M free_list_len=12k
```
Observation: evictions are low relative to allocs; reclaim counts are high but not matching the leak.

morgan: low evictions + rising active pages smells like fragmentation + small objects sticking in slab pools. Could be our slab allocator's size-class rounding after long-lived prefix caching. Any evidence of pinned refs (tool loop holding refs)?

noah: added a debug flag to log hold-count on page structs; saw a handful (~10-20) of pages with hold_count=1 for >30m. They had timestamps showing last_access from old sessions.

sarah: @morgan @devon FYI I pushed a micro-patch that makes the eviction scorer penalize pages with >5 minute idle but low reuse. Might help. Want to run a canary with that scoring to see if residency drops.

devon: canary SGTM. also let's try forcing aggressive compact on a repro to see if memory goes back down (`kvctl compact --aggressive --sleep 10m`). If compact frees a chunk, it's fragmentation. If not, likely leak refs.

kv-inspector-bot: Canary started on cluster redwood-canary-7 with patch kveviction/score-adjust-0.1. Rolling 3/3.

noah: running long-run with canary now. baseline run id=lr-091, canary run id=lr-092. I'll attach periodic jemalloc stats.

morgan: also check kernel selection path for that model — we changed blocked-simd kernel last week. Unlikely but worth verifying since the kernel swap changed per-token memory patterns (KV mapping done in host).

noah: quick jemalloc diff after 6h on canary: `allocated=1.9GB -> 1.76GB, active=2.2GB -> 1.95GB, metadata=210MB -> 198MB`. Nice drop but still small long-tail growth persists.

devon: promising. can you run the same but with `--kv-disable-cache` to make it purely compute-bound (no reuse). If growth vanishes, it's definitely cache-side.

noah: ran `--kv-disable-cache` for 8h. No sustained growth. So it's definitely KV-related.

morgan: next step: instrument pagechain walk to log when we decide not to evict due to "likely-reuse" heuristic. Add sampling at 1% to avoid overhead.

noah: did that; early logs show many page candidates skipped because heuristic predicted reuse, but actual access timestamps show no reuse for >20m. Looks like our LRU-ish recency estimator is biased by a few outlier sessions that hammer same keys, keeping global recency counts inflated.

sarah: that matches a hypothesis: heavy skewed keys inflate recency counters and protect unrelated pages through the sampler. We should factor per-session recency and global recency separately.

devon: agree. short term: reduce protection threshold and add age-decay to recency score. Long term: per-session occupancy and avoid global hot keys dominating eviction policy.

noah: I tested manual tweak: age-decay factor 0.6 applied every 5m. After 12h, active pages stabilized ~1.85GB and slab_frag_percent down to 10.8. Not perfect but an improvement.

morgan: good. Can we ship the eviction scoring change behind a runtime flag and run on canary for 72h? Also add a guard to prevent aggressive churn when load spikes (batching heuristics should avoid thrash).

noah: created PR #4821 with feature flag `KV_EVICT_DECAY_V2`. Included telemetry counters: pages_evicted_by_age, pages_protected_by_hotkey, avg_page_age_ms.

kv-inspector-bot: PR #4821 passed unit + integration checks. Canary rollout scheduled.

sarah: action items: (1) run canary 72h, (2) gather periodic jemalloc & slab stats, (3) run `--kv-disable-cache` sanity on a host each 24h to rule weirdness. I'll own dashboarding.

devon: also add the sampler logs to ephemeral trace (1% sample) and post to /mnt/tmp/kv-samples for offline analysis.

noah: thanks all — will post final canary numbers tomorrow. If we see stabilization we can promote patch to prod with flag off by default.

morgan: nice detective work. :mag: :thumbsup:

noah: quick note for the ticket: root cause likely combination of global recency bias + slab fragmentation; mitigation: recency decay + eviction score tweak.
